Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

basic adjective

fundamental, elementary

also the basics, basics, fundamental, elementary, rudiments, first principles, elements (of a subject)

classical

Hor. S. 1.1.26: elementa … prīma
Cic. de Or. 1.163 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 28: basics, elementa

elementa, elementōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural · Declension on Wiktionary

the basics, the ABC, first principles

Properly the letters of the alphabet, then the first lessons of any art; the very basics are prīma elementa (Hor. S. 1.1.26; Quint. 1.2.26).

Other words

  • prīmus, prīma, prīmum — basic, first, elementary (of lessons, rules, needs)

    adjective · classical · Tac. Dial. 30.1: prīma discentium elementa; Quint. 2.5.1: prīma rhētoricēs rudīmenta (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Latin says “first” where English says “basic”. Basic needs are the things ad vīctum necessāria (cf. Cic. Fam. 14.20; see necessary).

  • rudīmenta, rudīmentōrum n. pl. — first lessons, basic training

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Liv. 31.11 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 182: basic training, rudīmenta mīlitāria; Traupman 185 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Augustan and later (Lewis & Short), most often of a soldier’s first service.

  • fundāmentum, fundāmentī n. — foundation, basis

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.23: fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs · Declension on Wiktionary

    What everything else rests on, as a house on its foundations.

Examples

  • ut puerīs ōlim dant crustula blandī doctōrēs, elementa velint ut discere prīma

    as coaxing teachers sometimes give children biscuits, to make them willing to learn their ABCHor. S. 1.1.25–26

  • fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs, id est dictōrum conventōrumque cōnstantia et vēritās

    the foundation of justice is good faith: standing by what has been said and agreed, and telling the truthCic. Off. 1.23

See also simple, alphabet, learn, school.
